prompt:
TESSERA STYLE SHEET
1. Modern editorial paper collage. Bold magazine composition, refined 2D motion design.
2. One dominant flat block-colour background for the whole shot: soft violet. Never a rainbow, never a gradient.
3. Subjects are black-and-white halftone photographic cutouts with rough white torn-paper edges: objects, machines, buildings, maps, coins, screens, vehicles, anonymous paper hands. Never a recognisable person's face.
4. Diagram elements are flat matte paper shapes and ribbons in cream, black, pale yellow, or the background's contrasting colour. Real paper texture, print dots, small tape pieces.
5. Consistent upper-left light. Small paper-layer shadows only.
6. Everything is flat matte printed paper. No glow, no neon, no bloom, no halos, no luminous edges. Nothing emits light. Not glossy 3D. Not live action.
7. Headline typography: one extra-bold sans-serif, black or cream, printed on paper chips, large, safe margins. English spelling and letterforms accurate and stable. Only the headline text in the copy list, nothing else.
8. Motion: elements enter fast with slight overshoot and a stable landing, then hold a clear reading window. One strongest visual focus at a time. No camera shake. Movement starts on the first frame; a small loop continues at the end. No empty frames.
9. Numbers, when specified, are printed complete from their first visible frame. Never counting up, never morphing, never redrawn.
10. No brands, logos, watermarks, or text beyond the copy list.
11. 16:9, exactly 5 seconds, one composition, at most one crisp cut.
12. Identity anchor: rough white torn-paper edges on every cutout; small paper shadow from upper-left light.

BEAT
Ground: soft violet.
Subjects: the paper document; torn map pieces.
Opens on the document on screen, carried over from the previous shot, which transforms as the action begins.
Action: The document tears into torn map pieces that scatter and hold apart across the frame.
Ends holding on the scattered pieces.
Headline printed on a paper chip: "FRAGMENTED STANDARDS".

COPY LIST: "FRAGMENTED STANDARDS". Exact strings; nothing else appears in frame.

AUDIO: One English narrator, warm, clear, natural, brisk but unhurried, never an advertising shout. Speak the following line exactly once, word for word, beginning on the first frame: "ESG reporting stays fragmented, with standards varying across jurisdictions and industries.". No other dialogue. Light paper-slap and tape sound effects beneath the voice; no music.

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] This is a modern editorial paper collage in a 2D motion design style. <Picture 1> serves as the first frame, establishing a soft violet flat block-color background. The composition features black-and-white halftone photographic cutouts with rough white torn-paper edges, including a laptop screen and a layered paper document. Small paper-layer shadows are cast consistently from an upper-left light source. Every element has a flat matte printed paper texture with visible print dots and small pieces of adhesive tape. At 00:00.000, the central paper document suddenly tears apart with a fast, snappy motion, transforming into several jagged, torn map pieces. These pieces scatter outward across the soft violet ground with slight overshoot before landing in stable positions across the frame. Simultaneously, a new headline appears: a cream-colored paper chip with rough torn edges slides into the frame, bearing the extra-bold black sans-serif text "FRAGMENTED STANDARDS" in clean, legible English. A narrator (S1), a male with a warm, clear, and natural timbre and a brisk but unhurried speaking rate, begins speaking immediately: <d>[English] ESG reporting stays fragmented, with standards varying across jurisdictions and industries.</d> The camera remains in a Static Shot throughout the 5-second duration. By the end of the video, the scattered map pieces and the headline "FRAGMENTED STANDARDS" hold a clear reading window, with a very subtle, slow drifting loop to maintain visual life.

overall_soundscape: The audio is dominated by a clean, dry vocal recording. Beneath the voice, distinct diegetic sound effects of crisp paper tearing, sharp paper-slap impacts as elements land, and the tacky sound of adhesive tape being pressed occur in synchronization with the visual movements.
